Description: Name of what is measured or commanded.

What kind of interface the row is, which also fixes how Interfacing Equipment and Signal Owner relate. 

Measurement: state acquired by a controller from sensing hardware, including crew levers, selectors and pushbuttons; Interfacing equipement to Owner.

Command: hardwired drive of an effector or safety device; Owner to Physical; Analog or Discrete.

Request: setpoint, enable or mode asked of another controller over a data bus; Owner to Interfacing Equipment; Digital.

Computed: value derived by its owner, defined as an intermediate and derived state from other inputs. Interfacing Equipment empty.

Power: electrical supply, Owner is the source and Interfacing Equipment the load. See the Signal Role philosophy section in README.

Free-text connection or sensing technology note.
Physical interface kind. Drives Analog/Discrete/Power topology links when Physical ≠ Owner.
Engineering unit when applicable.
Lower end of the functional range of the quantity itself: the smallest value the interface is expected to carry in service. Independent of how it is encoded on any bus.

Upper end of the functional range of the quantity itself. Aircraft pitch may be functionally limited to 45 deg while the bus encoding allows 90 deg; the 45 deg belongs here and the 90 deg on the allocation row.

Derivation is filled whenever the value is produced by the owner's own logic: always for Computed, and for a Request whose value the sender computes. It stays empty when the owner relays a value unchanged, and for protocol fields such as freshness counters and CRCs.
